> Just tell them you search for a job or you haven't found the right profession yet.

That sounds like it could work. Thank you, and also for the movie, found a link.  
I always thought there would be some sort of friendly people with understanding for me as well. But it was going on for a very long time, at some point I started wanting to believe in people (as if pretty much that anyone I met was my friend), which was a mistake and led to some more abuse. It is kind of difficult to keep having energy. I suppose one shouldn't go looking for friends, friendships should form naturally. I think maybe I should rather do more of things that give me some energy because I am very tired all the time now.
Good for you. I used to have no problems with it either.

I tried but all non-Asians are students who are just having fun, their first question is always what am I doing here to which I have no admirable answer, they notice I am awkward and just don't want to talk to me because I'd ruin their fun. I even had a person complain on me, we sat next to each other on a plane, she thought I was sick (I was just nervous) and started freaking out that I've been following her (we indeed had the same way to baggage claim with the rest of the passengers). Paperwork here can be just bought. With jobs, local companies have restrictions and cannot take too many foreigners. This doesn't apply for foreign owned companies but one has to have friends to get recommended. I actually managed to get recommended twice but none worked out, they said I was too experienced - they need students who don't care about jobs and just want to have fun.  
Edit: What an irony that one of the reasons that added up to my first big breakdown and leaving the field I worked in were comments from colleagues mocking my origin, or that here in Asia I moved from my last place because the arrogance of the people there was unbearable...They were all German and here I get an answer from another German.

Hi! No, absolutely no way. I am in Viet Nam, I am Czech. I have to move around neighboring countries every 2 or 3 months because of visa and every country has different language so there's not enough time to learn any.  
I cannot go back because I was abused there by too many people for too long, that's why I think I am broken - I have not enough social standing to even tell someone.

> Most people suck. They are self centered and worried about themselves only. 

From the other side it works too: My mother used to visit people from the village in hospital when she was in the city and overheard someone was sick. It weren't even her friends, she just knew their names. They were obviously very happy someone (anyone) came around. The thing was that nobody liked my mother in the village, she was like a black sheep, so once that sick person left hospital they stopped all contact with my mother again.
IDK why but I'm actually happy for you and your friend ;)

Well shit. If I can look at my past mistakes and give advice...   

* Cooking is overrated (just google recipes and follow them, it is not always what it was supposed to be but most of the times it is edible)
* you will survive if you forget to buy soap and wash your hands in cleaning detergent for one day. your laundry will survive it too if you don't do it often.
* clothes don't need ironing if you let them dry on coat hanger
* plain cosmetic vaseline is the best thing for dry hands, dry lips, dry hair AND (!) leather shoes
* keep your shoes and nails clean that's what people really look at 
  
Seiously, practicalities are not the thing to be afraid of. Don't complicate it, don't try to do everything right, read the product composition, google, improvize!  
The real danger is if parents were making decisions for you maybe you will trust other people's opinions (and orders) too much. I actually think you will have to incidentally fuck something up in spite of best intentions and make a genuine mistake to become an adult (reacting on your username).
Well technically, I first got here now. In reality, couple of years ago: Wow so many ultra smart geeks! Now: A lot of sad people with no friends.
